statement: Width-based lower bound for (40a)/(8) using fixed variable order. The fixed-order width measure K_l fails the perfect matching control: perfect matching is in P but has exponential fixed-order OBDD width (experiment cm-f8ec3fb39cab47bd). Any lower bound proof using this measure would also 'prove' a false lower bound for perfect matching. The oracle-assisted version of Search-MCSP has polynomial width (MMW19 Thm 1.2 trie construction), so the 'hard property' (large width) does not even hold for the oracle version. The CHOPRS locality barrier is secondary - it only applies if width IS large but only locally so. The primary question is whether oracle-free Search-MCSP has large MINIMUM width over all orders (OBDD width).

statement: Sparsity of MCSP[N^beta] (|Im Eval| <= 2^{O(N^beta log N)}) as the candidate property P: REFUTED as a route to the Theorem R hypothesis. Reason: the sparsity bound is a counting fact about any language with few yes-instances, so it does not separate MCSP from languages where the reuse lemma fails. The known counterexample f(z,x)=z AND h(x) shows that sparsity plus projection stability does not give the intended elimination lemma (spec 'P != NP track - mandatory filters', F1; Q-142b3d067f known pitfalls). Filter F1 also caps the read-once width at S+1 for every cut, so no cut-rank measure built on sparsity can prove the streaming target.

statement: Projection stability (restriction of MCSP[N^beta] inputs to m' free variables, staying in MCSP at threshold (2^{m'})^beta) as candidate property P: REFUTED by control (1). Both controls satisfy it. (a) Parity_m restricted to m' free variables is parity_{m'} or its complement, with circuit size <= m'. (b) IP_n (2n variables) restricted to any subset of variables has a circuit of size <= 4n. Both remain yes-instances at threshold 2^{m'beta} whenever 4n <= 2^{m' beta}, i.e. m' >= log2(4n)/beta. Hence the property does not discriminate MCSP from parity/IP and by Proposition R1 cannot give c < 1. Scope: restriction-closure with the restricted threshold. Gap: other projection notions (existential projection onto a coordinate subset, random restrictions with a per-variable rate) are NOT covered and remain open.

statement: CORRECTION of my turn-13 entry (R0722, self-review not possible, flagged for independent review). statement: CORRECTION AND RELABEL (session R0713, turn 5). (1) The sparsity and projection-stability entries are FORMALIZATIONS refuted, not directions. Enriched variants stay open: existential projection onto a coordinate subset; per-variable random restriction; sparsity combined with an oracle-gate-local condition. (2) Turn-4 inference corrected: Proposition R1 (spec ACC0-MOD6 p.15) states only that a reuse lemma valid for ALL functions needs c >= 1 (parity witness). It does NOT by itself say that a property satisfied by parity and IP is excluded. The correct step is: if a candidate P of MCSP[N^beta] holds for parity and IP, and the lemma derived from P would give c < 1 for the parity witness, the lemma would contradict R1. So P must fail on parity or IP, or the lemma must be MCSP-specific. This is a CONDITIONAL reduction, not a refutation by R1 alone. (3) Self-reducibility formalization (downward: f|_{x_m=0} is an instance of the same problem at threshold (N/2)^beta; random: f(x+r)+f(r) linear structure): parity satisfies both trivially (parity_m|_{x_m=0} = parity_{m-1}; parity is linear, so f(x)=f(x+r)+f(r)). IP satisfies the same kind of linear-in-one-argument identity on each block. So the formalization fails control (1) and is REFUTED as a standalone P. Enriched open variant: self-reducibility that is NOT inherited by restrictions (e.g. reduction to MCSP at a different threshold with an explicit size loss), tested on parity/IP.

statement: CANDIDATE P_r with polylog threshold (r*(f) <= (log s)^k for some fixed k) is REFUTED by control (1). Reasoning only, pending independent review. Parity_m: the B2 XOR block (u = a OR b, v = NAND(a,b), out = AND(u,v)) gives a chain of size 3(m-1) in which each block output has fan-out 2, so r = m-2. With log s = beta*m and fixed k >= 2, m-2 <= (beta m)^2 for m >= 1/beta^2, so parity satisfies P_r. A property that parity satisfies cannot separate MCSP from parity, so by control (1) it cannot give c < 1.

structure.gap: The multilinear hitting-set lemma (Q-e988ea9656 LEMMA) uses sum_{i<=d} C(t,i) points. Any point set that hits the whole space of multilinear polynomials of degree <= d has at least that many points, since the evaluation matrix must have full column rank and the space has dimension sum_{i<=d} C(t,i). So the lemma is optimal for the full space. The TR26-313 target (cost s*t^{d-1-eps}) can therefore only come from using that the polynomial has a circuit of size s, i.e. a restriction to a structured subclass, not from a better point set for all degree-d multilinear polynomials. structure.lemma: REPAIR OF S0016 (LEMMA L0002). (a) For reals c>=1, eta in [0,1), beta>0, k>=0: (2+beta-eta)/(1+c) > 1+k*beta  iff  1-c-eta > (k(1+c)-1)*beta. Proof: multiply by 1+c>0 and rearrange. (b) For fixed c, eta, k, some beta in (0,1] satisfies the inequality iff c+eta<1 or 3-eta>(1+k)(1+c). Proof: g(beta)=(2+beta-eta)/(1+c)-1-k*beta is affine in beta. If g(0)>0 (i.e. c+eta<1), small beta>0 works by continuity. If g(0)<=0 and g(1)>0 (i.e. 3-eta>(1+k)(1+c)), beta=1 works. If both <=0, affinity gives g<=0 on [0,1], so no beta works. (c) The transfer step 'k is the exponent in CC(MCSP[N^beta]) > N^k from MMW19 Thm 1.4' is WITHDRAWN: the refutation shows Thm 1.4 has no such k. Parts (a),(b) are pure algebra and claim nothing about MCSP.

structure.proved_step: statement: Candidate lemma: Let X be a finite set of truth tables and let A subset X be the yes instances. Suppose a deterministic decoder D of the final state q(x) outputs none for x outside A and outputs a circuit C with Eval(C)=x for every x in A. Then q is injective on X. Proof: if x != y and q(x)=q(y), D returns the same output on both. If exactly one is in A, the output must be both none and a circuit. If both are in A, the same circuit would evaluate to both x and y, contradiction. Thus no distinct pair collides.
